head_object_reread.note: The head-object re-read agrees three ways with the content hash: the object's own content-sha256 metadata, its ContentLength, and the version id. The metadata is corroboration only; the digest that decided FOUND is the one computed from the downloaded bytes. Both versions were head-read at 19:10:08Z and 19:10:13Z respectively; the ETag and the object content-sha256 metadata recorded for each come from those reads at their full length.

noncurrent_expiry.read_from: s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration on opal-313476888478-lambda-artifacts. The bucket HAS a lifecycle configuration, so the answer is not NoSuchLifecycleConfiguration, but it holds exactly ONE rule -- abort-incomplete-mpu-7d, Enabled, empty prefix filter -- whose only action is AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload after 7 days. There is NO NoncurrentVersionExpiration and no Expiration action of any kind, so nothing in the configuration would expire the found noncurrent-capable version. Stated as rule_present false because the question is specifically about a rule that expires NONCURRENT versions, and there is none; the MPU-abort rule is recorded here so the reading is not mistaken for 'no lifecycle at all'.
noncurrent_expiry.consequence: No row is owed to the issuer on this point: the found version is not at risk from a lifecycle rule. It is the LATEST version today, and it would only become noncurrent if something else were uploaded to the same key.
